solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: English party goer who'll make his mark?

parts.note: a raver is someone who goes to wild parties

explanation.surface: A partying Englishman expected to leave a lasting impression on the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make his mark' is literal for this definition: someone who cuts marks into metal or glass.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan who incises designs or lettering into a surface quite literally leaves marks on it.

clue.text: News broadcast proclaiming international peace?

definitions.meaning: a long-running BBC Radio 4 lunchtime news programme has this title
read literally, the phrase announces that the whole globe is in harmony

explanation.surface: A bulletin announcing that nations have finally stopped fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a famous British radio news programme, and taken word by word it describes global unity.

clue.text: Risk gentle walk after end of spring

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word spring

parts.note: an amble is a slow, leisurely stroll

explanation.surface: Taking a chance on a relaxed stroll once spring is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the stroll behind the single letter from spring.
explanation.definitionFit: To risk something is to take a chance or bet on an uncertain outcome; the verb senses match.

clue.text: Lawyers for boxers, perhaps

definitions.meaning: barristers' cases are given to them on instruction documents, and slang uses the word for the lawyers themselves
boxer shorts are one kind of men's underpants

explanation.surface: Legal representatives acting on behalf of prizefighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxers' suggests fighters needing lawyers, but here it means a style of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls counsel by the name of their case papers, and underpants of a short style share the same plural noun.

clue.text: Shocking weather

parts.note: shocking in the literal electrical sense: lightning and thunder make the weather full of voltage

explanation.surface: A complaint about appalling conditions outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A thunderstorm with lightning is weather that is literally charged with electricity, hence shocking.

clue.text: Try to sell bird of prey

definitions.meaning: to peddle goods noisily in the street or door to door
a raptor such as a goshawk or sparrowhawk

explanation.surface: Someone attempting to flog a raptor.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to peddle wares, and the noun names a sharp-eyed raptor.

clue.text: Girl needing three different articles

parts.note: together with the next two words this gives three grammatical articles; the first is the indefinite one used before a vowel
the second article, the definite one
the third article, the indefinite one used before a consonant

explanation.surface: A young woman who needs three distinct items.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'three different articles' asks for three distinct grammatical articles, an, the and a, strung together.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so a girl's name stands in for the girl herself as is usual in crosswords.

clue.text: Refill gun with bullets or lead, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of 'or lead' might be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Putting fresh ammunition into a gun, whether bullets or lead shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ORLEAD; 'lead' looks like ammunition but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging a firearm again with fresh ammunition is the exact sense of the verb.

clue.text: Sketched rotating components of power drill

indicators.note: rotating says the hidden letters are read backwards
components of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Describing the spinning parts of an electric drill.
explanation.walkthrough: WERD sits across 'power drill'; 'rotating', apt for a drill, turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of the verb for making a picture with pencil, a synonym for sketched.

clue.text: Muscular men complain, given something sweet to eat

parts.note: to beef is slang for to grumble
a cake is a sweet baked treat

explanation.surface: Fit men grumble but are pacified with a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for displays of male physique, especially brawny men in photographs.

clue.text: Love rhymes, when abroad

parts.note: love is a zero score in tennis, shown as the letter O
rhyming lines are verse
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Writing romantic poetry while travelling in foreign lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs describe being in a foreign country, across the sea.

clue.text: A church service

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Simply a religious service held in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' is not worship here but a tennis serve the receiver cannot touch.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a serve the opponent fails to return at all is an outright winning service.

clue.text: Pair initially ignoring British people

indicators.note: the leading letter, standing for British, is dropped from the front of the word for pair

parts.note: a brace is a pair, especially of game birds

explanation.surface: A couple who first ignore British people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially ignoring' removes B from the front of BRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A people in the sense of an ethnic group or nation, which is one sense of the noun.

clue.text: Telephone service out of order in chalet

indicators.note: out of order says the letters of 'in chalet' are jumbled, apt for a broken phone

explanation.surface: The phone at the ski chalet is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' looks like a faulty phone but scrambles INCHALET.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone number callers ring to talk with others, a kind of telephone service.

clue.text: In favour of daughter initially getting nudge

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word daughter

explanation.surface: Supporting a daughter who is being gently prompted.
explanation.definitionFit: To poke or push someone lightly, as a verb or noun, is a synonym of nudge.

clue.text: Protest: Conservative traitor is US politician

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
a rat is a betrayer or turncoat

explanation.surface: A protester calls a Conservative a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of one of the two main American parties, the one with the donkey emblem.

clue.text: Lack thread for spinning

indicators.note: spinning, apt for thread, says the letters are whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: Not enough thread for the spinning wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' looks like textile work but rearranges THREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarcity or shortage of something, a synonym for lack as a noun.

clue.text: Vehicle test taken by girl's relative

indicators.note: taken by links the test to the girl who sits it, putting the possessive after it

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for cars in Britain
her is the possessive for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl's relative sits her driving or car test.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT (Ministry of Transport test) is Britain's yearly roadworthiness check for cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent is a close family member, so this is a specific example of a relative.

clue.text: Shorten written agreement

definitions.meaning: to make smaller or draw together, the verb sense
a formal legally binding document, the noun sense

explanation.surface: Instructions to cut down a signed deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to reduce in size; the noun is a legally binding deal on paper.

clue.text: Took lady out every now and then? Right

indicators.note: taking letters out every now and then picks the even letters of 'Took lady'

explanation.surface: Someone asks for confirmation that they occasionally took a woman on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out every now and then' picks the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal ways of agreeing or saying something is acceptable or correct.

clue.text: Story — end section read aloud

indicators.note: read aloud says the word is said so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: the tail is the hind or end part of something

explanation.surface: A story's final part is read out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read aloud' fits a story, but it signals a sound-alike: TAIL said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative or yarn, a straightforward synonym for story.

clue.text: Is unable to scan notes in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is unable to scan their notes.
explanation.definitionFit: The negative modal verb means lacks the ability, matching is unable.

clue.text: Turbulent R. Niger not following expected course?

indicators.note: turbulent, apt for a river, says the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: The rough waters of the River Niger stray from their usual course.
explanation.definitionFit: Straying from the right path, morally or literally, so a wandering river fits the question-marked definition.
